speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; to begin our evaluation, have you noticed any recent changes in your coordination, balance, or speech patterns?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description of appearing "drunk" while walking and feeling clumsy on the right side suggests cerebellar involvement. To better localize the lesion, have you noticed any slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, or tremors?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy, given the history of uncontrolled Crohn's disease, recent onset of right-sided cerebellar ataxia, and the known association between natalizumab and JC virus reactivation.
